recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆分葉核嗜中性球的細胞質邊緣（箭頭）有一小團深紫色顆粒狀包涵體（morula），背景血小板稀少，配合蜱蟲叮咬與血小板低下，符合無形體症（anaplasmosis）。
features: Segmented neutrophil with a small dense basophilic granular intracytoplasmic inclusion at the cell periphery (arrow)
Inclusion is distinct from the nuclear lobes and has a stippled morula-like texture
Neutrophil cytoplasm with fine pink granules
Normocytic, normochromic red cells with rare crenated forms
Very few platelets in the field, in keeping with thrombocytopenia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic erythrocytes and a paucity of platelets. A segmented neutrophil contains a small, dark basophilic, stippled intracytoplasmic inclusion separate from the nuclear lobes, consistent with a morula. No intraerythrocytic parasites are seen. In a patient with a recent tick bite, fever and thrombocytopenia, findings are consistent with human granulocytic anaplasmosis; PCR confirmation and co-infection testing (Babesia, Borrelia, Powassan virus given neurologic symptoms) are recommended.

ddx.vs: Ehrlichia chaffeensis morulae are located in monocytes rather than neutrophils.
Döhle bodies are pale blue-grey, amorphous and homogeneous rather than dark and stippled.
Babesia parasites are intraerythrocytic rings and tetrads, not neutrophil inclusions.

ddx.dx: Detached nuclear fragment or overlying platelet
ddx.vs: A platelet or nuclear fragment has a different texture or focal plane and lacks the granular mulberry appearance.
